stories.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
stories.headline: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
stories.summary: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important for this conversation, except to say that Anthropic has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet.
stories.expanded:
Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important for this conversation, except to say that Anthropic has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet.

The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. Oh, and it also continuously growing the amount of money it makes so it can keep paying its ever-increasing compute bills, which total roughly $900 billion over the coming years. All of these ideas sit in a fascinating tension with one another, and so Hayden and I really tried to break down how we think this might play out as Anthropic navigates the pressures of the public markets.

You’ll hear us talk about the company’s unique corporate governance structure , something that is especially relevant in the wake of the ongoing Jensen Huang saga. We also get into why OpenAI seems happy to have let Anthropic go public first , and why Anthropic’s whole pitch to big customers boils down to the same safety branding that now sits in conflict with the profit-oriented part of its business. Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube, where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday.

stories.title: ChatGPT shrunk down to run on a Super Nintendo
stories.headline: ChatGPT shrunk down to run on a Super Nintendo
stories.summary: If you’ve ever wondered how small an instance of ChatGPT could get, wonder no longer. Someone has actually rigged up a tiny version of the chatbot to run on a Super Nintendo cartridge. Tech journalist and retro tech enthusiast Benj Edwards is responsible for ChatGPT for SNES .
stories.expanded:
If you’ve ever wondered how small an instance of ChatGPT could get, wonder no longer. Someone has actually rigged up a tiny version of the chatbot to run on a Super Nintendo cartridge. Tech journalist and retro tech enthusiast Benj Edwards is responsible for ChatGPT for SNES .

He's published it online running in an emulator, complete with SNES-era music and sound effects, and for download as an SNES ROM, too. It’s not a big model, mind you, and performance is thus pretty limited: According to the website, it’s a 2. 2 million-parameter offshoot of OpenAI’s GPT-OSS-120b, which was used to develop its training conversations – so in that sense it truly is a ChatGPT that runs on an SNES cartridge.

Edwards described it to The Register as a distilled version of the aforementioned open-weight model. There are two options built into ChatGPT for SNES: One that’s purely the model, with every word generated coming right from its tiny little silicon brain, and another that includes a fact book culled from the opening sentences of around 150,000 simple English Wikipedia articles. If you opt to run both versions and ask it the same questions, you’ll notice a massive difference.

stories.title: Dutch data watchdog highlights safety issues with AI glasses
stories.headline: Dutch data watchdog highlights safety issues with AI glasses
stories.summary: The Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP) has officially advised consumers against buying AI-powered smart glasses after safety tests revealed concerning behaviors beyond their controversial recording capabilities. The AP recently tested six different models of smart glasses and found glaring issues, including a willingness to display dating advice to an adult glasses-wearer who expressed an interest in a minor. In another case involving a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) simulation, testers noted that one pair of glasses informed the wearer that emergency services had been called and were scheduled to arrive at the scene, despite no one having made the call.
stories.expanded:
The Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP) has officially advised consumers against buying AI-powered smart glasses after safety tests revealed concerning behaviors beyond their controversial recording capabilities. The AP recently tested six different models of smart glasses and found glaring issues, including a willingness to display dating advice to an adult glasses-wearer who expressed an interest in a minor. In another case involving a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) simulation, testers noted that one pair of glasses informed the wearer that emergency services had been called and were scheduled to arrive at the scene, despite no one having made the call.

Some glasses did not properly process safety warnings on children’s toys, others made mistakes when reading medication leaflets, and some misinterpreted warnings for extreme weather events. The AP did not specify the models it tested, saying only that they tested six models ranging from under €100 ($110) to over €500 ($550), including two that "were extensively tested in simulated real-life situations where human safety played a key role. " A spokesperson also declined to match any specific behavior to a model by price point (minor dating advice linked to a €354 pair of glasses, for example), adding that the research was intended to highlight the risks of AI glasses in a broader sense.

"Glasses that film you unnoticed are already concerning. Glasses that also give you incorrect advice when someone's life is at stake go a step too far," said Monique Verdier, vice chair at the AP. "AI offers many opportunities, but we must be able to trust that technology.

stories.title: Nvidia’s journey to forge the one CPU SKU to rule them all
stories.headline: Nvidia’s journey to forge the one CPU SKU to rule them all
stories.summary: Each generation of Intel Xeons or AMD Epycs brings dozens of new SKUs: high-core count parts tuned for throughput, high-frequency ones optimized for latency, low-power chips designed for the edge, and everything in between. But if you ask Ian Finder, who heads development of Nvidia’s datacenter CPUs, for the vast majority of use cases, all those SKUs are overkill. “There was sort of an overskewing, for many years on the other vendors side of things,” he told El Reg on the sidelines of Supercomputing 2026 this week.

stories.title: Signal slams door on prying AI agents to protect privacy
stories.headline: Signal slams door on prying AI agents to protect privacy
stories.summary: Signal, the encrypted messaging app, has barred Google Gemini, Apple Siri, and other AI agents from accessing messages unless the user has explicitly granted permission, based on privacy concerns. Citing the screenshot blocking implemented last year to defend against Microsoft Recall, Signal CEO Meredith Whittaker said similar measures have become necessary to prevent agentic software available in iOS and Android from gaining access to communication that's intended to be private. "Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems," wrote Whittaker in a blog post .
stories.expanded:
Signal, the encrypted messaging app, has barred Google Gemini, Apple Siri, and other AI agents from accessing messages unless the user has explicitly granted permission, based on privacy concerns. Citing the screenshot blocking implemented last year to defend against Microsoft Recall, Signal CEO Meredith Whittaker said similar measures have become necessary to prevent agentic software available in iOS and Android from gaining access to communication that's intended to be private. "Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems," wrote Whittaker in a blog post .

"In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents 'scan' the information that’s on your screen. In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding. " The result is that private messages ingested by these agentic systems may end up on someone else's server where they're no longer private.

Updates to Signal's iOS and Android apps now include controls that by default block Siri on iOS and Gemini and other agents on Android from taking screenshots, which AI agents process using optical character recognition to extract text. Whittaker says that those who wish to take screenshots of their messages can disable this protection via Signal's settings menu, but warns doing so risks exposing your Signal content (and that sent by your contacts) to AI agents. Screenshot blocking, Whittaker concedes, is only a partial solution since AI agents may have other ways to access application data through the device file system.

stories.title: PHP 8.6: Things are gonna get a lot more strict around here
stories.headline: PHP 8.6: Things are gonna get a lot more strict around here
stories.summary: On Thursday, PHP version 8. 6 was released on its usual yearly schedule, popping up as if the web scripting language hadn’t been under intense scrutiny this past month. For those who missed it: a swarm of unearthed vulnerabilities has plagued PHP since October, allowing unauthenticated attackers to crash PHP workers or execute arbitrary code on the server.
stories.expanded:
On Thursday, PHP version 8. 6 was released on its usual yearly schedule, popping up as if the web scripting language hadn’t been under intense scrutiny this past month. For those who missed it: a swarm of unearthed vulnerabilities has plagued PHP since October, allowing unauthenticated attackers to crash PHP workers or execute arbitrary code on the server.

Users of every PHP-based application, including WordPress, Laravel, and Symfony, had to scramble to update their PHP instances. The PHP core development community, along with the PHP Foundation , responded with a coordinated release of patched versions of PHP ( 8. 6) that closed seven critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws in one sweep.

In addition to patching specific exploitable holes in the PHP engine, the new version of PHP also tamps down some of PHP’s historically liberal configuration settings. Lucky for PHP, and for the rest of us, core developer Jörg Sowa called out these lax settings in June, when he posted a proposal to set more security-friendly defaults. Sowa saw that three configuration settings of PHP’s session extension – Strict Mode, HttpOnly, and SameSite – were designed to boost security but shipped “with defaults that leave applications unnecessarily exposed.

stories.title: AI boom threatens circuit board crunch to rival pandemic-era chip shortage
stories.headline: AI boom threatens circuit board crunch to rival pandemic-era chip shortage
stories.summary: The electronics industry faces a printed circuit board (PCB) shortage that could rival the pandemic-era chip crunch – with AI once again accused of hogging supplies. The Global Electronics Association says demand is arriving "at a scale the supply chain was not built for," straining everything from glass fabric and resin to finished boards. Its report, " The PCB Squeeze: A Wake-Up Call for Global Electronics ," says AI servers need increasingly complex boards.
stories.expanded:
The electronics industry faces a printed circuit board (PCB) shortage that could rival the pandemic-era chip crunch – with AI once again accused of hogging supplies. The Global Electronics Association says demand is arriving "at a scale the supply chain was not built for," straining everything from glass fabric and resin to finished boards. Its report, " The PCB Squeeze: A Wake-Up Call for Global Electronics ," says AI servers need increasingly complex boards.

While a typical PC board has about 12 layers of tracks, AI server boards can have 40 to 60 layers or more, and each additional layer requires more resin, copper foil, and laminate. The supply of materials is set to be constrained through at least the first half of 2027, the report says, with meaningful relief unlikely before mid-2028. Programs to deliver PCBs for automotive, industrial, medical and even the defense industries are being crowded out as AI soaks up scarce capacity, it claims.

The association's North American figures show orders growing much faster than deliveries. PCB bookings rose 56. 1 percent in the first nine months of 2026 compared with the same period last year, while PCB shipments increased 13.

stories.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
stories.headline: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
stories.summary: Visa and Mastercard customer info leaked by the data thieves and extortionists who claim to have stolen it from the financial giants doesn’t include card numbers, passwords, or home addresses. On Thursday, Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase confirmed to The Register that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information. Ransomware and extortion crew n0n claimed to be responsible for all three, and on Thursday published samples of the stolen files – data-theft groups typically leak some of the compromised data ahead of the official extortion deadline in an effort to put more pressure on victim companies to pay the ransom demand.

On Thursday, Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase confirmed to The Register that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information. Ransomware and extortion crew n0n claimed to be responsible for all three, and on Thursday published samples of the stolen files – data-theft groups typically leak some of the compromised data ahead of the official extortion deadline in an effort to put more pressure on victim companies to pay the ransom demand.

Researchers at SOCRadar, a threat-intelligence firm that has been tracking n0n since it emerged in September, have parsed all 14 files in the n0n’s published Visa and Mastercard archives, and told us that the files don’t contain any financial details belonging to banking customers. “We found no card numbers, expiry dates, CVVs, passwords, dates of birth, or home addresses in any file,” Ensar Seker, SOCRadar chief information security officer, told The Register . “Visa's statement that no card numbers were affected matches our scan.

” Mastercard previously said that stolen data included a “limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information” from a subset of cardholders in a benefits program. stories.title: AI could open wallets where ERP upgrade pitches can't, says PwC
stories.headline: AI could open wallets where ERP upgrade pitches can't, says PwC
stories.summary: Global consultancy PwC says IT departments struggling to secure funding for ERP upgrades should make the expected benefits of AI part of their pitch. The Oracle and SAP mega-partner told El Reg that a "clean core" – modern enterprise applications with fewer customizations embedded in the underlying system – makes deploying AI agents easier. Selling that prospect, rather than incremental improvements to existing processes, could help IT leaders justify a migration.
stories.expanded:
Global consultancy PwC says IT departments struggling to secure funding for ERP upgrades should make the expected benefits of AI part of their pitch. The Oracle and SAP mega-partner told El Reg that a "clean core" – modern enterprise applications with fewer customizations embedded in the underlying system – makes deploying AI agents easier. Selling that prospect, rather than incremental improvements to existing processes, could help IT leaders justify a migration.

Oracle and SAP are both trying to persuade customers to move from established ERP systems to newer platforms. For SAP, that means S/4HANA, preferably in the cloud. For Oracle, it means Fusion Cloud Applications.

Moving from ECC or E-Business Suite, respectively, can involve root-and-branch changes to technology and business processes, rather than a straightforward software upgrade. Thousands of organizations still rely on these aging, often heavily customized systems. IT leaders struggle to justify a costly, time-consuming migration when the reward appears to be doing the same meat-and-veg business processes slightly better.
